C1.rationale: Level 2: Clear communication of complex interdisciplinary concepts across diverse audiences, and collaborative group research discourse.
evidenceLines: Communicate and justify complex concepts and results clearly and effectively to a variety of audiences.
Plan and engage in sustained critical investigations and evaluations of research topics both independently and as part of collaborative groups.

C2.rationale: Level 3: Interdisciplinary problem solving reconciling mind-brain-behaviour philosophies with empirical neurobiology and deductive logic.
evidenceLines: Understand and evaluate a variety of philosophical and scientific traditions about the relationship between brain, mind, and behaviour, including cross-cultural perspectives.
Display excellence in critical thinking, including the ability to critically evaluate a variety of inductive and deductive arguments.

C3.rationale: Level 3: Rigorous critical evaluation of inductive and deductive arguments, primary scientific literature, and disciplinary hypotheses.
evidenceLines: Engage in critical review of appropriate and relevant information sources.
Display excellence in critical thinking, including the ability to critically evaluate a variety of inductive and deductive arguments.

C4.rationale: Level 2: Formulating sustained research investigation plans and designing interdisciplinary experimental inquiry frameworks.
evidenceLines: Plan and engage in sustained critical investigations and evaluations of research topics both independently and as part of collaborative groups.
Show familiarity with discipline-specific experimental approaches, simulations and research methodology.

C5.rationale: Level 3: Independent investigative research inquiry integrating neuroscience simulations, experimental protocols, and philosophical analysis.
evidenceLines: Plan and engage in sustained critical investigations and evaluations of research topics both independently and as part of collaborative groups.
Show familiarity with discipline-specific experimental approaches, simulations and research methodology.

W1.rationale: Level 1: Academic laboratory exposure and foundational application of critical reasoning to general workplace contexts.
evidenceLines: Such skills in critical thinking are integral to the discipline of philosophy. They are also tremendously useful in other academic domains, in the workplace, and in everyday life.
Content will be delivered in lectures and laboratory-based classes.

W2.rationale: Level 2: Evaluative judgment regarding cross-cultural traditions, underlying epistemological assumptions, and ethical philosophical reflection.
evidenceLines: Understand and evaluate a variety of philosophical and scientific traditions about the relationship between brain, mind, and behaviour, including cross-cultural perspectives.
critically analyse one’s opinions at an introductory level to identify underlying assumptions and unforeseen consequences (especially assumptions or consequences that are open to objections);

evidenceLines: Show familiarity with discipline-specific experimental approaches, simulations and research methodology.
The course provides in-depth exposure to the cellular mechanisms utilised by neurons.
